fixture_adjustment_case1.why_not_softening_the_defect: This is compose-file plumbing unrelated to the planted defect (checkout-api's http.Client{} with no Timeout). It was tripped by a genuine TortureU/compose interaction, documented below, not by anything about the defect itself.
fixture_adjustment_case1.interaction_found: internal/run's R-EXE-20 rename mechanism disables the original internal-dependency service via a compose profile that is never activated. `docker compose up` treats a profile-disabled service referenced by another service's `depends_on` as an undefined service and hard-fails validation before starting anything -- observed directly: 'service "checkout-api" depends on undefined service "dep": invalid compose project'. This would affect any real docker-compose.yml using the extremely common depends_on-on-an-internal-dependency pattern, once R-EXE-20's rename actually engages for that dependency (which, before the Defect C fix, it never did for a non-vocabulary host -- so this interaction was previously unreachable and is only now exposed). Reported as a finding; not patched (out of scope).

case8_control_repeated_runs.conclusion: Re-confirmed clean on the corrected (unioned) classification path. Zero findings, 8/8.

case1_no_timeout.what_actually_happened: The fault fires correctly this time (Defect B and C both hold): markers arrive, the proxy is correctly wired to the renamed dep-tortureu-backend, and the 3s latency toxic genuinely reaches the SUT's traffic. k6 itself measured this correctly and wrote a complete --summary-export file BEFORE exiting -- recovered directly from the run's temp directory: http_req_duration median 2915.6ms, p95 3004.4ms, p90 3003.5ms (unmistakably the 3-second toxic hitting the majority of requests), threshold p(95)<1000 correctly computed as crossed. But k6 exits with status 99 (its own standard, documented exit code meaning 'thresholds were crossed', not a crash), and internal/run/load.go's K6Runner treats ANY non-zero k6 exit as a load-generator failure -- `cmd.Wait()` returning an error sends the error down h.errCh unconditionally, in both host-process and container-mode paths, without ever attempting to read the summary file that k6 already wrote successfully.
case1_no_timeout.conclusion: The planted defect WAS detected by k6's own measurement, but TortureU's own process-exit handling throws the result away and reports status:error ('the tool broke') instead of status:fail ('the SUT broke') -- for precisely the case E1 exists to test: a real, correctly-measured threshold breach.

defect_D.title: K6Runner discards k6's --summary-export result whenever k6 exits non-zero, including k6's own normal exit code for 'thresholds crossed' (99) -- so a genuine, correctly-detected SUT failure is reported as a tool error instead of a verdict
defect_D.severity: critical and central to E1: this means status:fail with real findings can never be produced via a k6 threshold breach at all, for any torture.yaml, in any case where the SUT genuinely fails an SLO under load -- which is the corpus's entire premise.
defect_D.root_cause: internal/run/load.go's K6Runner.startHostProcess and K6Runner.startContainer both do: `waitErr := cmd.Wait(); if waitErr != nil { h.errCh <- waitErr; return }` before ever reading summaryPath. k6 exits 99, not 0, whenever any threshold's condition is not met -- this is k6's own long-documented convention, not a crash or setup failure -- yet the summary file is still written completely and correctly in that case (confirmed: read directly off disk after this exact run, see case1_no_timeout above). K6Runner never distinguishes 'process never produced a summary' (a genuine load-generator failure) from 'process produced a complete summary and then exited 99 because k6's own threshold gate fired' (the expected, desired signal for a real defect).
defect_D.empirical_confirmation: Case 1 run, this round: verdict JSON says status:error / 'load generator failed: exit status 99' with zero findings; the summary file recovered from the same run's temp directory shows a complete, correct measurement of the planted 3-second latency defect (p95 3004ms against a p(95)<1000 threshold).
defect_D.owner: internal/run/load.go (K6Runner) -- out of this task's edit scope. Reported, not patched. The evident fix shape (not implemented here): attempt to read and parse the summary file regardless of cmd.Wait()'s error, and only surface waitErr as a load-generator failure if the summary is missing or unparseable.
